name: Volare
headline: Every part of the journey, connected.
summary: A corporate travel platform connecting trips, flights, hotels, policy, approvals, and spend across web and native iOS.
why: Travelers need a clear next step. Operations and finance need the same picture, especially when plans change.
detail: I bring the traveler experience and the operational work behind it into one product: trip planning, group travel, exceptions, and the context needed to support people along the way.

name: Grid
headline: A company that is easier to navigate.
summary: An employee home for company resources, people, teams, org structure, office information, and everyday answers.
why: Finding the right person or document should not depend on knowing which channel to ask in.
detail: Grid gives scattered company information a useful front door. People, resources, and places belong together because that is how employees experience the company.

name: Grep
headline: Find the answer. Keep the evidence.
summary: A company search and intelligence workspace for finding decisions, prior work, source material, and the people behind them.
why: Useful answers need traceable sources and the right access, not another layer of information to sort through.
detail: Grep brings retrieval, synthesis, and company context into a workspace built around questions people actually ask. The source remains part of the answer, so the next decision has something solid behind it.

name: Support Station
headline: Turn customer signals into coordinated action.
summary: A support workspace connecting queue health, customer sentiment, quality, reporting, knowledge gaps, and incident response.
why: Support teams need to see what needs attention and connect individual issues to patterns across the product.
detail: Support Station brings operational context and AI-assisted analysis into the same place. The aim is to help engineers, managers, and leaders understand the situation, investigate recurring issues, and coordinate the response.

name: Counsel
headline: Give legal judgment a better workspace.
summary: AI-assisted contract review bringing clause triage, playbooks, redlines, precedent, and negotiation context into one workspace.
why: Legal teams need the relevant evidence beside the clause they are reviewing, with control over every decision.
detail: Counsel organizes the work around the contract: compare a clause with the playbook, review a proposed change, and retain the reasoning and history. AI helps prepare and surface context; the lawyer stays in charge of review.

name: Revenue Copilot
headline: Less assembly. More informed next steps.
summary: A shared workspace for revenue priorities, pipeline, forecasts, account research, and AI-assisted daily work.
why: Teams should be able to act on account context without rebuilding it from disconnected systems every morning.
detail: Revenue Copilot brings work queues, research, analytics, and team visibility together. Numbers and recommendations retain their source context, so the team can understand what it is acting on.

name: PULSE
headline: Your Replit workspace, within reach.
summary: Chrome and Raycast companions for app building, project access, and permission-aware project insights.
why: Bring useful context into the tools people already use, so getting to the work takes fewer steps.
detail: PULSE connects desktop and browser workflows with Replit. The surrounding release hub gives employees a clear place to get the companions and understand what changed.

name: Hireflow
headline: Put recruiting context in one place.
summary: A hiring workspace connecting sourcing, candidate search, screening evidence, recruiter calibration, and ATS workflows.
why: Recruiters need consistent context and a clear way to inspect the evidence behind a recommendation.
detail: Hireflow brings the steps around a role into a shared workflow, from discovering candidates to reviewing their supporting material. Recruiter judgment and calibration are part of the product.

name: Asset Lab
headline: Connect the brief to the usable asset.
summary: An AI-powered brand and asset workspace for generating, organizing, and working with launch and marketing material.
why: Creative work needs a path from an idea to something the team can find, reuse, and put to work.
detail: Asset Lab brings creation and asset management together. Brand context, generation, and organization sit within the same workflow instead of being scattered across separate tools.

name: Kaishi
headline: Keep the thinking. Move the work forward.
summary: Meeting capture, searchable transcripts, decisions, and actions brought into a dedicated workspace.
why: A good conversation should leave context people can recover and a next step they can follow.
detail: Kaishi began with the need to preserve the value of a standup. It connects what was said with the actions and project context that follow, and informed the development of the broader Studio workbench.

name: Vibecode Time
headline: Make building something everyone can join.
summary: An internal platform for build challenges, themes, submissions, voting, and sharing what employees make with Replit Agent.
why: People learn what AI can do by using it on a real idea and seeing what their colleagues create.
detail: Vibecode Time gives company building events a home, from joining a challenge to submitting a project and discovering the work. Enablement becomes something people participate in.

name: AI Studio
headline: Give the work behind the products a home.
summary: A portfolio workbench for requests, projects, meetings, feedback, tasks, and reviewed priorities across the Studio.
why: As the portfolio grows, requests, ownership, evidence, and follow-through need to stay connected.
detail: The workbench brings Studio coordination into one place while source applications keep their own records and access boundaries. It is being developed through a pilot, with rollout and team adoption treated as separate milestones.
